papers.title: Constitutively active presynaptic release factor Unc13A prevents homeostatic sleep rebound in Drosophila.
papers.summary: Expressing a constitutively active, Ca2+/calmodulin-insensitive form of the presynaptic release factor Unc13A (Unc13AWRWR) in Drosophila nearly eliminated homeostatic sleep rebound after acute sleep deprivation while leaving baseline sleep largely intact. A genetic modifier screen identified partial loss of αSnap, an NSF cofactor for cis-SNARE disassembly, as a suppressor of the reboundless phenotype, implicating a balance between SNARE complex assembly and recycling in sleep homeostasis.

papers.title: Stress-recovery dynamics reveal a separatrix in transcriptomic landscapes across organs and aging
papers.summary: Young and aged mice were subjected to transient sleep deprivation, and transcriptomes from six organs were profiled immediately after stress and after recovery to map age- and organ-dependent temporal dynamics. Neural ordinary differential equation-inferred transcriptomic vector fields revealed distinct stability regimes, including a separatrix in young testis transcriptomes that bounds the region from which perturbed states can return toward control.

papers.title: Aperiodic dynamics track cortical state shifts during sleep K-complexes
papers.summary: Using time-resolved spectral parameterization of overnight sleep EEG, the study characterized aperiodic dynamics around expert-annotated K-complexes (KCs) with controls to separate genuine cortical state shifts from waveform artifacts. A component of the KC-locked aperiodic change survived these controls, indicating that KCs are accompanied by a genuine shift toward a higher-exponent, inhibition-dominated cortical state.

papers.title: A systems-level model of sleep-dependent memory-consolidation failure in neurodegeneration: the spindle-slow-oscillation decoupling cascade dissociates amyloid and tau
papers.summary: The authors built a systems-level model coupling cortical slow oscillations, thalamic spindles, and hippocampal ripples to cortical spike-timing-dependent plasticity, and used it to simulate sleep-dependent memory consolidation failure in neurodegeneration. They report that spindle-slow-oscillation timing, not oscillation power, gates consolidation, and that amyloid and tau produce orthogonal signatures (amyloid collapses slow-wave power while sparing replay order; tau the reverse) across the amyloid × tau plane, with a falsifiable prediction that closed-loop slow-oscillation enhancement rescues memory only for coupling/amplitude-dominated deficits.

papers.title: Best Practices in EEG Analysis: Preprocessing, Modeling, and Machine Learning
papers.summary: Provides a practical and methodological guide to modern EEG analysis, covering preprocessing, artifact removal, statistical modeling, connectivity, source localization, machine learning, and reproducibility. Emphasizes best practices for reliable, interpretable, and reproducible EEG pipelines, including cross-subject generalization, data leakage, and FAIR data practices.

papers.title: Sleep macro-architecture in sleep-deprivation-sensitive and sleep-deprivation-insensitive juvenile myoclonic epilepsy: A polysomnographic study.
papers.summary: Overnight polysomnography compared sleep macro-architecture in juvenile myoclonic epilepsy (JME) patients with versus without self-reported sleep-deprivation-triggered seizures and in healthy controls. Sleep-deprivation-sensitive JME patients showed lower N3 and reduced REM than controls, and sleep-deprivation-sensitive status independently predicted N3% after adjustment for sex and anti-seizure medication class.

papers.title: Cardiac responses to auditory irregularities reveal hierarchical information processing during sleep
papers.summary: The authors analyzed electrocardiography responses to auditory local-global deviants during wakefulness and sleep in 56 participants to test whether cardiac signals index hierarchical sensory processing. They found cardiac slowing after global deviants specifically during REM sleep, especially tonic REM, and cardiac acceleration effects restricted to light NREM sleep, suggesting cardiac responses can inform state-dependent hierarchical information processing during sleep.

papers.title: Sleep and circadian regulation of DNA repair and retrotransposons in neuronal genome stability and neurodegenerative disease mechanisms.
papers.summary: This review synthesizes evidence that sleep and circadian rhythms temporally regulate neuronal genome stability, focusing on clock-dependent DNA repair pathways, sleep-related chromosomal integrity, and sleep-wake-dependent retrotransposon activity such as LINE-1. It proposes that sleep provides a permissive state for genome-protective processes and discusses links to neurodegenerative disease, noting that much human evidence remains preclinical or correlative.

papers.title: [Microstructural characteristics of sleep electroencephalogram in obstructive sleep apnea].
papers.journal: Zhonghua er bi yan hou tou jing wai ke za zhi = Chinese journal of otorhinolaryngology head and neck surgery
papers.summary: This case-control study of 1,821 suspected OSA patients analyzed sleep EEG microstructural features and found that OSA patients exhibited increased PSD across multiple frequency bands and stages, with trends intensifying by severity, alongside higher slow wave oscillation density/duration/amplitude in N3 and lower sleep spindle density in N2, indicating cortical hyperarousal and thalamocortical dysregulation.

papers.title: Regional and network patterns of sleep-depth-associated brain diffusion changes: an EEG-informed multishell diffusion MRI study.
papers.summary: In 9 healthy adults who maintained sleep during simultaneous EEG and multishell diffusion MRI, deeper sleep (lower ORP) was associated with reduced white-matter fractional anisotropy and kurtosis fractional anisotropy, lower gray-matter diffusivities, and opposite kurtosis effects, with region-specific correlations forming a network primarily in frontocentral and medial frontal-cingulate areas.

papers.title: Sleep fragmentation frequency is associated with distinct immune, microbial, and barrier-related profiles in DSS-induced colitis in mice.
papers.summary: In DSS-induced colitis mice, low- and high-frequency sleep fragmentation were associated with distinct endpoint-specific profiles: both increased plasma corticosterone, while high frequency increased colonic Th2 proportions and low frequency increased MPO, without significant corrected differences in clinical colitis severity among DSS groups.

papers.title: Validation of a dual 2-back task as an effective method for inducing acute mental fatigue.
papers.summary: This study validated a novel dual 2-back task for inducing acute mental fatigue in 73 healthy young adults over 30 minutes of continuous visuospatial working memory updating. Participants showed increased fatigue and sleepiness, reduced detection performance (d'), decreased P300 amplitude, and increased alpha power, while frontal theta and cardiac pre-ejection period reactivity remained stable, indicating the task effectively induces mental fatigue without increased boredom.

papers.title: The circadian clock regulates KCNH2 (hERG) promoter activity through daily temperature rhythms.
papers.summary: The authors tested whether the human KCNH2 (hERG) promoter is a direct transcriptional target of the circadian clock using luciferase reporter constructs in C2C12 myotubes under serum shock or temperature cycling (36.5–38.5°C). They found a conserved tandem E-box required for promoter oscillation and BMAL1:CLOCK-dependent transactivation, and that dominant-negative CLOCKΔ19 reduced hKCNH2 promoter amplitude under temperature cycling without altering period, concluding that daily temperature rhythms regulate KCNH2 promoter activity through the circadian clock.

papers.title: Quadratic associations between harsh parenting and changes in children's nightly sleep.
papers.summary: This longitudinal study examined quadratic associations between harsh parenting at age 9 and changes in children's sleep over 2 years in 329 children. Greater declines in sleep minutes, efficiency, and increased sleep activity were observed as harsh parenting increased from low to moderate levels, with associations attenuating at higher levels, demonstrating non-linear relations.

papers.title: A retrospective exploratory study of sleep spindles as an adjunctive diagnostic marker for narcolepsy type 1: a comparison with insufficient sleep syndrome.
papers.summary: This retrospective study compared sleep spindle indices from overnight polysomnography in 14 patients with narcolepsy type 1 (NT1) and 9 with insufficient sleep syndrome (ISS) to differentiate them. Automated detection found significant between-group differences in C3 fast spindle duration during N2 and density during NREM sleep, with C3 fast spindle duration showing moderate discriminatory performance (AUC 0.754, sensitivity 85.7%, specificity 66.7%), suggesting automated spindle quantification may complement MSLT.

papers.title: P-body sequestration of clock transcripts delays repressor synthesis to set circadian period in Drosophila
papers.summary: Using time-resolved proximity labeling, a behavioral RNAi screen, and single-molecule RNA-FISH in Drosophila clock neurons, this study identified P-body components Me31B and Pacman as regulators of circadian period. Sequestration of per and tim transcripts in P-bodies delays translation and repressor synthesis, whereas Pacman-dependent decay terminates repression; Me31B overexpression lengthened the free-running period by approximately 2 hours.

papers.title: Dietary selenium deficiency drives sex-specific circadian disturbance through redox imbalance and causes early systolic dysfunction in mice
papers.summary: Mice fed a selenium-deficient diet for 12 weeks showed reduced plasma selenium, early systolic dysfunction via reduced global longitudinal strain, and cardiac transcriptomic changes enriched for redox, mitochondrial, and circadian pathways. These effects were sex-specific, with a more pronounced cardiac stress response in males.

papers.title: Nocturnal behaviours, stridor and recurrent respiratory failure in anti-IgLON5 disease.
papers.summary: This case report describes a 77-year-old woman with anti-IgLON5 disease who presented with obstructive sleep apnea, recurrent hypercapnic respiratory failure, and elaborate nocturnal behaviors, initially misdiagnosed as epilepsy. Serial polysomnography showed progressive loss of sleep spindles and undifferentiated NREM sleep; she partially improved with intravenous methylprednisolone and rituximab, highlighting the need to test for anti-IgLON5 disease in treatment-resistant sleep-disordered breathing.

papers.title: Sleepiness assessment tools for predicting fitness to drive: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
papers.summary: This systematic review and meta-analysis of 61 studies assessed the predictive ability of sleepiness assessment tools for impaired driving performance. Both subjective (KSS) and objective measures (PERCLOS-80, KDS, EEG alpha/theta power, microsleep episodes) were robustly associated with impaired driving, but certainty of evidence was low to very low, and predictive utility requires further investigation.

papers.title: GA Eases Atherosclerosis by Regulating Circadian Rhythm.
papers.summary: In ApoE-/- mice fed a high-fat diet, glycyrrhetinic acid (GA) reduced serum IL-6, TNF-α, LDL-C, TG, and TC and increased HDL-C. RNA-seq and qPCR identified upregulation of circadian clock genes Per1, Per2, and Per3 in aortic tissues, suggesting that GA's anti-atherosclerotic effects may involve circadian rhythm-related signaling.

papers.title: Integrative genetic analyses of circadian chronotype and autism highlight regional co-association at 17q21.31.
papers.summary: Integrative genetic analyses (LDSC, SMR, MR, colocalization) of chronotype and autism spectrum disorder found a negative genetic correlation and exploratory regional co-association at 17q21.31, with colocalization favoring distinct variants over a shared causal variant. Eveningness-oriented IVW MR was positive but attenuated with robust estimators, and no mediation through sleep duration or insomnia was detected.

papers.title: The orexinergic system in Alzheimer's disease: from sleep disruption to accelerated neurodegeneration.
papers.summary: Reviews the role of the orexinergic system in Alzheimer's disease, linking sleep-wake dysregulation to amyloid-beta accumulation and neurodegeneration. Highlights preclinical and biomarker evidence, and discusses the potential of orexin-targeting interventions, though proof of disease-modifying effects remains limited.

papers.title: Stage-specific neural correlates of how personal and observational experiences affect risky decision-making: an exploratory EEG study.
papers.summary: Using a sequential risk-taking task and EEG, this exploratory study found that personal experience was linked to larger frontal P2 amplitudes and higher decoding accuracy, while observational experience was linked to greater reward positivity (RewP) during feedback. The results suggest partially shared but stage-specific neural processing for personal versus observational risk information.

papers.title: Distinct EEG functional network alterations in Parkinson's disease and multiple system atrophy.
papers.summary: EEG functional connectivity was compared across 28 Parkinson's disease (PD), 42 multiple system atrophy (MSA), and 27 healthy controls. MSA showed β-band amplitude-based hypoconnectivity, while PD showed phase-based decoupling in δ and β bands; adding these features to clinical assessments gave a modest exploratory gain in discriminating PD from MSA-P.

papers.title: Multidimensional neuropsychological heterogeneity in obstructive sleep apnea: deep clinical phenotyping in a single-center cohort, population proteomic context, and depressive-burden risk stratification.
papers.summary: This study integrated clinical phenotyping, UK Biobank proteomics, machine learning, and PBMC transcriptomics in obstructive sleep apnea (OSA). Cognition was associated with apnea burden and TyG, while affective burden was more strongly associated with TyG; a depressive-burden risk model achieved cross-setting AUROC up to 0.809, though calibration was less stable, and 21 proteins were shared across cognition, depression, and anxiety outcomes.

papers.title: AAV-mediated TBR1 replacement ameliorates behavioral and electrophysiological abnormalities in Tbr1-haploinsufficient mice
papers.summary: Evaluated AAV-mediated human TBR1 supplementation in Tbr1-haploinsufficient mice after a single postnatal day 3 retroorbital injection (2E11 vector genomes). Treatment increased TBR1 protein and TBR1/CTIP2/parvalbumin cell counts, improved sociability and food-seeking behaviors, and attenuated elevated relative theta power and social-interaction EEG abnormalities, though anterior commissure abnormalities and some EEG/sleep deficits persisted.

papers.title: Interpreting heart rate variability in clinical context: a framework for understanding a multidimensional autonomic biomarker.
papers.summary: This review summarizes the physiological basis and acquisition methods of heart rate variability (HRV) and proposes a context-aware framework for interpreting HRV as a dynamic signal rather than a standalone diagnostic marker. It emphasizes that HRV interpretation is influenced by measurement modality, duration, circadian timing, behaviors, medications, and comorbidities, and may complement cardiovascular risk assessment when appropriately contextualized.

papers.title: [Daytime sleepiness with recurrent nocturnal fall-related injuries: a case report of somnambulism triggered by severe obstructive sleep apnea].
papers.journal: Zhonghua jie he he hu xi za zhi = Zhonghua jiehe he huxi zazhi = Chinese journal of tuberculosis and respiratory diseases
papers.summary: This case report describes a 34-year-old man with severe obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) who experienced somnambulism episodes and false-positive MSLT results. CPAP therapy eliminated somnambulism episodes, normalized sleep architecture, and corrected the MSLT result, suggesting that vPSG should be performed before MSLT in patients with sleepiness and abnormal nocturnal behaviors.

papers.title: Resting-EEG Characteristics and Classification Model Exploration for Tap Test Prediction in Communicating Hydrocephalus: A Small-Sample Pilot Study.
papers.summary: This pilot study used resting-state EEG to predict tap test responsiveness in 30 patients with communicating hydrocephalus. Responders showed higher alpha-band power correlated with CRS-R improvement, and linear models (logistic regression, SVM) achieved high AUCs (up to 0.982), matching or exceeding deep learning models, indicating that EEG spectral features are linearly separable and sufficient for prediction.

papers.title: Impact of REM sleep deprivation during the acquisition phase on learning and memory performance, neurotrophic and oxidative stress markers in male rats.
papers.summary: REM sleep deprivation during the acquisition phase in adolescent male rats impaired Morris water maze probe trial memory and increased anxiety-like behavior, accompanied by elevated corticosterone, reduced hippocampal TAS, SOD, and NGF, and increased TOS. The findings link REM sleep disruption with altered memory performance, oxidative balance, and neurotrophic markers.

papers.title: Correlation between perinatal asphyxia-induced brain injury, number of enlarged perivascular spaces, and sleep quality in later life.
papers.summary: In 319 neonates with perinatal asphyxia, the number of enlarged perivascular spaces (EPVSs) independently correlated with the severity of brain injury across all infants and in mild and severe subgroups. In the severe asphyxia group, higher EPVS counts were associated with worse long-term sleep quality, suggesting EPVSs as a biomarker for injury severity and future sleep disturbances.

papers.title: Sleep and circadian rhythm characteristics in unaffected first-degree relatives of individuals with schizophrenia and bipolar disorder.
papers.summary: This cross-sectional study compared sleep quality, chronotype, and biological rhythms in 146 participants (44 relatives of schizophrenia patients, 47 relatives of bipolar disorder patients, and 55 controls). No significant group differences were found in overall sleep quality, chronotype, or biological rhythm measures, though relatives reported later habitual bedtimes and wake-up times, suggesting circadian characteristics are largely preserved in unaffected first-degree relatives.

papers.title: A context-aware temporal modeling through unified multi-scale temporal encoding and hierarchical sequence learning for single-channel EEG sleep staging.
papers.summary: Proposes TempoSleep, a context-aware framework for single-channel EEG sleep staging that combines multi-scale feature extraction with temporal modeling and uses class-weighted loss and data augmentation to address class imbalance. Achieves 89.72% overall accuracy and 85.46% macro F1-score, with a notable 61.7% F1-score for the N1 stage on SleepEDF datasets.

papers.title: CIRCADIAN CLOCK ASSOCIATED 1 Expression Responds to High Temperature Precisely Through Alternative Splicing in Arabidopsis.
papers.summary: This study shows that Arabidopsis CIRCADIAN CLOCK ASSOCIATED 1 (CCA1) responds to high temperature gradients through alternative splicing, with CCA1βab isoforms upregulated at moderate high temperatures and CCA1 globally upregulated at extreme high temperature. The temperature-dependent shift in CCA1βa-to-CCA1βb isoform ratio fine-tunes biotic stress defense and reactive oxygen species homeostasis, supporting thermal adaptation while preserving circadian stability.

papers.title: Recommended sleep duration is associated with greater parasympathetic regulation in patients with hypertension.
papers.summary: In 74 hypertensive patients, those achieving recommended sleep duration (7-9 h) had significantly greater 24-hour high-frequency heart rate variability (parasympathetic activity) than short sleepers (<7 h), independent of age, sex, dyslipidemia, β-blocker use, and physical activity energy expenditure. The findings suggest adequate sleep supports autonomic regulation in hypertension.

papers.title: Association between minimum nocturnal heart rate and cerebral small vessel disease in patients with obstructive sleep apnea.
papers.summary: In a retrospective study of 630 patients with obstructive sleep apnea, 42% had cerebral small vessel disease (CSVD). Older age and higher nocturnal minimum heart rate were independently associated with CSVD, with a model AUC of 0.752, indicating that elevated nocturnal minimum heart rate, possibly reflecting autonomic dysfunction, is linked to CSVD in OSA.

papers.title: Event duration, endotypes and hypoxic burden in obstructive sleep apnoea.
papers.summary: This study examined the association of respiratory event duration with OSA severity and endotypes in 1008 Asian patients with moderate-to-severe OSA. During NREM sleep, longer event durations were associated with higher arousal threshold, greater upper airway collapsibility, lower compensation, longer circulatory delay, and increased hypoxic burden, while AHI alone did not adequately reflect hypoxia-related disease burden.

papers.title: The effects of coherent breathing and blue light after an acute stress on sleepiness and the stress response in a workplace setting: A randomized double-blind cross-over trial.
papers.summary: Evaluates a workplace stress management intervention combining 0.1 Hz coherent breathing and blue light exposure in a randomized double-blind crossover trial. The intervention significantly reduced subjective stress by 31.23%, decreased sleepiness by 0.84 points, and increased positive affect by 1.85 points, with no significant effects on negative affect or HRV.

papers.title: Lactobacillus reuteri ATG-F4 alleviates behavioral impairment induced by chronic stress.
papers.journal: The Korean journal of physiology & pharmacology : official journal of the Korean Physiological Society and the Korean Society of Pharmacology
papers.summary: Chronic stress in mice increased immobility frequency and reduced locomotor and exploratory behavior, while Lactobacillus reuteri ATG-F4 treatment maintained immobility at control levels, restored locomotion and exploration, reduced stress-enhanced sleep latency, and modulated brain expression of GABA and serotonin receptor genes and gut microbiota composition. The results indicate ATG-F4 ameliorates chronic stress-induced behavioral impairments, potentially via gut-brain mechanisms.

papers.title: β-Lactam-Induced Encephalopathy: An Underrecognized Complication Of Commonly Used Antibiotics-A Case Report.
papers.summary: A 67-year-old man with septic shock developed encephalopathy (minimal consciousness, agitation, myoclonus, dyskinesia) during treatment with multiple β-lactam antibiotics; symptoms resolved after discontinuation and recurred upon re-exposure to structurally distinct β-lactams, supporting a class effect even without severe renal failure. This case highlights β-lactam-induced encephalopathy as an underrecognized adverse drug reaction.

topic.label: Sleep Homeostasis
topic.description: Sleep pressure, recovery, circadian interactions, and longitudinal regulation of NREM/REM sleep.
